current_example.problem: Let $F(x)=x^3 - x + 5\cos x$ for $x\in[0,\pi),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **even** extension of $F(x)$ to $x \in (-\pi,\pi).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in(-\pi,0)?$
current_example.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in[0,\pi),$ the even extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14121869/assets/0b4d33840ea40cea57ba69bf7c86e262ce44cd2db782ff0fee10b2890e2057de.svg)

In our cases, for $x\in(-\pi,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =F(-x) \\  & =(-x)^{3}-(-x)+5\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x) \\  & =-{x}^{3}+x+5\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
